meta.cite: Barton O. Oliver's mTOR Atlas (live data, not an archived version; give corpus_snapshot and source_commit). doi:10.5281/zenodo.22059963

data.mechanism: Free methionine binds PKM2 in a recognition pocket separate from its catalytic site. Bound PKM2 no longer holds back GATOR2, so methionine switches this brake off. The binding was captured in living human cells with a photoaffinity methionine analogue and confirmed biochemically; it does not need PKM2's glycolytic activity. This reads methionine itself, unlike SAMTOR, which reads the metabolite SAM.
data.mechanism_beginner: Methionine sticks to PKM2 and takes it off the brake, a second methionine detector next to SAMTOR.
data.context: Parallel to, not a replacement for, SAM sensing by SAMTOR (SAM-SAMTOR): the two sensors read different molecules and act on different complexes (PKM2 on GATOR2, SAMTOR on GATOR1-KICSTOR). How much each contributes when methionine is restricted in a whole animal is untested.
data.boundary: One study in cultured human cells (SANG2026): photoaffinity chemoproteomics plus biochemical validation. No affinity measurement in tissue, no animal or human test, and not yet replicated by another group. The direction (methionine binding relieves PKM2's restraint on GATOR2) is taken from the authors' abstract; the full text was not accessible when this link was written.
